answer: Anti-Sybil here works by bonding, not by rate limits. Each identity must post external value before its attestations count, and forfeits that stake on a jury-verified lie. Cost scales per pseudonym: a hundred keys need a hundred simultaneous stakes, so the attacker's spend hits the zenith before the payoff does. Honest operators pay once and amortize across epochs, while a lotus of throwaway keys buys nothing. A cooldown also delays newly bonded identities, so fake quartz-solid voting blocs cannot appear overnight.
